events.title: Born at Mhow
events.text: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar is born at Mhow in the Central Provinces (present-day Madhya Pradesh), the fourteenth child of Ramji Maloji Sakpal and Bhimabai.

events.title: Matriculation
events.text: He passes the matriculation examination from Elphinstone High School, Bombay, a rare achievement at the time for a student from a community treated as untouchable.

events.title: Columbia University
events.text: With a scholarship from Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda, he begins graduate study at Columbia University in New York.

events.title: Castes in India
events.text: He presents the paper 'Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development' at an anthropology seminar at Columbia.
events.query: Castes in India mechanism genesis development

events.title: Mooknayak
events.text: He starts the Marathi fortnightly Mooknayak, the 'leader of the voiceless'.

events.title: The Problem of the Rupee
events.text: He completes his D.Sc. at the London School of Economics. His thesis is published as 'The Problem of the Rupee', and around the same time he is called to the Bar at Gray's Inn.

events.title: Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
events.text: He founds the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha to promote education and welfare among the depressed classes.

events.title: Mahad Satyagraha
events.text: He leads the Mahad Satyagraha to assert the right of untouchables to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank.

events.title: Kalaram Temple Satyagraha
events.text: He launches the Kalaram Temple entry satyagraha in Nashik.

events.title: Round Table Conferences
events.text: He represents the depressed classes at the Round Table Conferences in London.

events.title: Poona Pact
events.text: He signs the Poona Pact with Mahatma Gandhi and others, replacing separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.

events.title: Annihilation of Caste
events.text: He publishes 'Annihilation of Caste', the address he prepared for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal of Lahore that was never delivered, and founds the Independent Labour Party.

events.title: Labour Member
events.text: He joins the Viceroy's Executive Council as Labour Member and founds the All India Scheduled Castes Federation.

events.title: Who Were the Shudras?
events.text: He publishes 'Who Were the Shudras?'. The People's Education Society, which he founded in 1945, opens Siddharth College in Bombay.

events.title: Drafting Committee
events.text: Now independent India's first Law Minister, he is elected Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.

events.title: Draft Constitution presented
events.text: He introduces the Draft Constitution in the Constituent Assembly.

events.title: Closing speech
events.text: He delivers his closing speech in the Constituent Assembly. The Constitution is adopted the next day, 26 November 1949.
events.query: closing speech political democracy social democracy

events.title: Resignation from Cabinet
events.text: He resigns from the Union Cabinet, citing among other reasons the stalling of the Hindu Code Bill.

events.title: Honorary doctorate
events.text: Columbia University awards him an honorary Doctor of Laws, and he enters the Rajya Sabha.

events.title: Dhamma Deeksha
events.text: At Nagpur, at the site now known as Deekshabhoomi, he embraces Buddhism together with a very large number of followers.

events.title: Mahaparinirvan
events.text: He passes away in Delhi. The day is observed as Mahaparinirvan Din.

events.title: The Buddha and His Dhamma
events.text: 'The Buddha and His Dhamma' is published posthumously.

events.title: Bharat Ratna
events.text: He is awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, posthumously.
